item.title: Re: A strange foundation(seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Although this does seem intriguing I don't really like most of the ideas presented here. Also, for the page layout, you can just say there will be multiple iterations of the article that are still gonna be readable. This Foundation being made up entirely of anomalies themselves that only contain what we perceive as regular animals (maybe if you explored the reason they contain them and revealed that the wildlife are actually anomalies or something we aren't aware of) is something I could bite on. The rest I don't like.

You say they have one(1) site but then immediately tell us about three(3) different ones. Not to mention you stated that their language was impossible to decode but then say that they establish communication and talk with our Foundation? What do you mean by multiple terminations? Like did the Foundation just casually wipe out this Foundation multiple times or their entire species and they just keep popping back up? I have no idea why our Foundation would merge with this Foundation, at the most I think our Foundation would just establish an alliance-ish thing with them. They're pretty much useless to the Foundation and unless they pose an actual threat or can help the Foundation at all besides just abducting cows then I don't really see how that would happen.

this Foundation also has almost nothing in common with our Foundation besides containing wildlife instead of anomalies so I don't really know that attention grabber makes sense

item.title: Re: seeking greenlight: ehe birh (didnt mean to post twice)
item.content:encoded:
Sorry, but this is just a pile of cliché SCP tropes. Not only do these birds have telepathy, but can also end the world just because. The way you described the concept is also a bit confusing. If you somehow build a very intriguing story to make up for the concept, then MAYBE it'll stand a chance. I also need to bring attention to your English. It seems like you struggle a bit to describe what you want to do, so maybe you'll have to improve on that first because clinical tone is difficult.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Retro-Causality and You
item.content:encoded:
Since I haven't been on the forums in a while and this grabbed my attention I guess I'm gonna take a crack at this.

+ show block
– hide block

The Tests(not in the idea critique) can be cross-referenced with the statements from the SCP to uncover what happened. Statements of |||||||||| is text that has been scratched out beyond recognition

I'm not exactly sure what you mean by this? Are basically saying that although what happens won't be outright stated, it can be solved if you just pay a bit more attention? That isn't a page format, it's probably just something that should go in the elevator pitch or central narrative. I have no idea what to say about the |||||||||||| part. Are you trying to talk about a redaction? You can just say that you don't need to show it.

Dealing with retro-causality and how to test an anomalous object that can change the past.

  • Testers have issues discovering how the SCP functions since it wipes people's minds and rewrites history and records the instance of the change.

That is almost the whole idea of SCP-140, a book about the Daevites that rewrites history and details this in the book whenever it's given blood or something (I honestly don't remember), not just in the book but also in our real world. Although people's minds aren't wiped they don't take notice, until they notice it. Not to mention there are countless time-space-changing-cognitohazard books out on the mainlist. So your base concept has already been done. Also, this elevator pitch is hella short lmao.

  • Book was discovered to have been placed into SCP containment by someone who might have known the book's anomalous properties.

Alright. But how was this placed into containment? Did they just plop it into an empty containment cell? There aren't just spare cells up for use on the daily when someone does a flick of the wrist. How could this person have even put it in containment? Who is this person? Are they even central to the anomaly or are they just there to conveniently drop this good old book off for reading at their nearest site? Does this even add anything to the anomaly? Shouldn't this be in the elevator pitch??

  • Unfortunate Accident causes it to end up in the research department

"Unfortunate Accident causes it to end up in the research department".. Okay. I'm not even gonna ask what that even means because this still literally tells me nothing about the anomaly or the concept. Do you think the Foundation just let these things sit in their neat containment cell while the security guards and researchers sit around and eat pringles all day? Isn't it standard that these anomalies end up in the research department regardless of anything?

  • Marion Wheeler discovers and returns the book back to containment.

Oh my god. Hold the phone bro. Marion Wheeler? Why is he even here? I just scrolled down and you don't even mention him again, what is he even adding to this. You know what, alright. How would he have discovered the book if the book was already in containment?? Why would he need to return the book to containment, isn't it already in containment, why would researchers even have to take it out of containment..????? Shouldn't all of this be in the elevator pitch as well..

  • Testing begins

OK.

  • Containment Breach by a D-Class individual using the book during a test.

Didn't you just say that the book wipes the minds of everyone that reads it? How would the D-Class even use the book, it changes the past, not the present, so it can't be used to blow a hole to freedom, is this gonna be presented as an elaborate scheme where the D places something to help him escape in the present in the past with the book? It's not like the D is gonna have access to the book at all times, it's not even guaranteed that a D-Class works with an anomaly more than once. Can it just be influenced to change the past on the fly?

Content Summary-

….Dude the hook/attention grabber section isn't used for this. This should all be in either the elevator pitch or central narrative, even the format of this is disjointed and jumbled all over the place. THIS WHOLE SECTION DOESN'T EVEN TELL ANYONE WHY THEY SHOULD BE INTERESTED IN THIS.

While within 5 meters of SCP-####. Do not speak or write any untrue statements. In an emergency, you can talk in future tense but you must not make any statement about the past or present (specifically opinions or statements that are false or have the possibility of being false)

The 5 meters tells us nothing about the anomaly, in fact, most of what I've already nitpicked doesn't even elaborate on what the anomaly does beyond being a book that changes the past, and if it's just that I already told you the concept has already been done before.

In an emergency? What does talking about future tense even do? Again you've never elaborated on any of this. Now the book can change shit about the present. Man, how are you gonna contradict your idea and change it mid-way through. The reason I've been so harsh with this is because some of these sentences make NO SENSE because you haven't given context where it should and the fact that you have this concept and format all over the place. How can an opinion be false?? What does any of this mean??????

The text of SCP-#### is a range of statements about our world. More recent statements have been able to be verified as true. So far, no statements have been verified as false.

This just raises more questions for me, if none of the statements are false then wouldn't the book would just be considered to be a book with weird stuff in it? How would the Foundation even detect the mind-erasing and history-changing? Btw you can just refer to the SCP as SCP-XXXX and not ####.

I'm not gonna do a line by line for the rest because I'm gonna drive myself mad. Also, chill with the redactions and black-boxing, it's not intriguing and it'll probably just make people feel like they're gonna have a stroke reading that or not make anything out at all. Also the way you're describing the "Containment Summary" and "Description Summary" (which summary is literally a synonym for description) just makes it look like you separated two things that should probably be put in one paragraph for no reason.

Like I said, I have no words for the rest cause it's legit just random text. You bulleted almost everything when you should only bullet things in the elevator pitch. I'm sorry if it seemed that I was a bit rude and rough when it came to the crit but I just want to be brutally honest. As it stands I don't think the idea would make it on the mainlist and if it did it would probably just go into deletion. I hope you come up with some more ideas because even if you don't always think up bangers instantly I do think every author deserves a chance.

item.title: Re: The Three Sided Coin
item.content:encoded:
I haven't come up with its exact origin story yet, but I had a general idea that its very old and can adapt its non-anomolous sides to whatever currency is most prevalent in the time of each specific tale. So like in colonial times it could look like a shilling, in Europe it could look like a euro, in my first tale it looks like an American quarter. This is mostly just to keep it from being detected and to help it blend in no matter when or where someone has it.

The monster is an enlarged version of the person with the coin with 2 rows of sharp teeth, 5 spikes on its head in the shape of a crown (maybe the origin story could trace it back to some ancient king?). It would have redish skin and extra long arms that end in flesh and bone scythes that it uses to decapitate its victims. The transformation only lasts until the monster has finished off its victim(s), then they revert back to their normal human selves. I need to transfer the tale into my sandbox but then ill post a link for it.

Also, thanks for checking out my thread!

item.title: Re: A strange foundation(seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
While this does seem interesting in concept, the fact there are many different versions of the Foundation from different dimensions is pretty much already established and done before, more than once. I'm a big fan of multiverse-type stories, so if you could think of a way to make this more unique and have it stand out from the other articles with a similar concept, then I would happily greenlight this. However, as it stands now, it feels pretty bland and barebones. You didn't describe any sort of actual narrative, just what happens after the Foundation discovered the alternate Foundation.

What I do like about this is how the other Foundation contains normal animals instead of anomalous creatures, so you should expand upon that. Why are they containing normal animals? What ARE the normal animals in their universe?

Please work on this more

item.title: Re: The Three Sided Coin
item.content:encoded:
I'm not sure if I'm supposed to have separate threads for my tale and my scp article if the tale is about the scp. But I realized I didn't explain what happens in my first tale.

Edit to Central Narrative: The tale is about a man who come into a western town after being robbed and has essentially nothing. Then he meets a strange man in a bar who loves gambling, buys him dinner and drinks, and talks about his lucky coin. The two spend the night drinking and betting on coin flips with each other until sunrise. As they're watching sunrise we learn the man with nothing is a wanted man and the strange man forces him to make a bet on a flip of the coin. If he wins the man with nothing can have the strange man's horse and get out of town, if he loses the strange man can turn him in for the bounty. But on this flip the coin lands on its anomalous side, transforming the strange man into the monster, which then attacks the man with nothing.

The monster is a transformed version of whoever flips the coin, but they grow bigger and gain spikes on their head, extra pointy teeth and have long arms with boney scythes where their hands should be.

item.title: Re: it's all in your head (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
TL;DR - I think that this idea is somewhat interesting and has the potential to become a good article, but I don't think it's quite at that point yet.

+ show block
– hide block

As znaegele said in their feedback on your idea, at the stage that the idea is currently at I don't think there is enough to distinguish it from other similar articles (035 comes to mind). There are certainly articles that have been done regarding the alteration of the article itself (3939) and articles that include elements of disguising an anomaly's true nature (3651), but I will acknowledge that you have a unique combination here. It may be that a forum post is not enough to fully describe your idea, which is completely understandable, and if you have a sandbox page you could DM me on the IRC I would be happy to take a deeper look. As for specific points to work on, I think that some elaboration on the struggle between the host and the parasite as the article is being written could do a lot. How did the researcher acquire the parasite? Why is the researcher allowed to write the article when controlled by this parasite? When does the Foundation take notice? How is the article successfully written, or is it even able to be completed in the first place (artifacts of several different editors editing the page with or without the parasite could add some nuance)?

Definitely don't toss this idea out, as I think it has the potential to be great. Good luck with your writings! :)

item.title: Malicious Magnet (seeking greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Similar to a standard SCP article, having 4 additional addendums that show testing logs.

Elevator Pitch: A floating, inanimate, red metal object that exhibits an anomalous magnetic force. It will work as a normal magnet when presented with most metal objects. However, it will alter its magnetic force when humans are around, causing pain (due to altering blood flow) or even death to individuals with things like pacemakers or prosthetic replacements. It will also destroy any technology that comes close enough using this force.

Central Narrative: The SCP was originally found in a meteoroid crash site. The anomaly was originally reported to the foundation because of the death of 3 individuals investigating the meteorite. It was relatively difficult to retrieve because it had torn the body armor of the MTF sent to investigate, causing major injuries to the chest area. It was eventually retrieved aircraft, towing it to containment through a long-distance hook.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I think this SCP has the potential for a lot of interesting testing and theorizing, and I don't think a sentient magnet concept has been done before.

Additional Notes: It is unknown if this SCP is sentient or not.

item.title: Re: Murderous Power Cord
item.content:encoded:
Did someone ask for a critique?

+Let's do it!
-Let's do it!

My initial thought to the title itself was, 'ah, so a power cord that strangles people like a snake.'
Turns out, I was correct. The electrocution part didn't surprise me since it's a power cord.

The fact that it gives vulgar death threats while killing people? Death threats vulgar and foul enough to induce nausea? I was not expecting that and I think that's pretty entertaining. Not drop dead hilarious, but definitely amusing.

The Central Narrative is disappointing, though. It essentially boils down to, 'it killed people before it was contained, I wonder where it came from?' and that doesn't satisfy.

Even though the merciless-deadly-killing-murdering-sentient-object thing has been done to death, the fact that it gives death threats is what makes it kinda stand out to me.

An anomaly is just a tool for a story to be told and any tool's mileage varies entirely on the person using it. I suggest fleshing out the plot and giving us specific scenarios and situations and a leading narrative and not just a short summary you gave. Also, try to find ways to make it funny. You have a sentient power cord that can strangle people and it gives extremely vulgar death threats. Use that to make people laugh.

Anywho, I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day! 👍

P.S. Usually, drafting should be saved for after Greenlights and not before, but the enthusiasm is good. It shows promise.

item.title: Alternate dimension where humans cannot fly above a certain altitude
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Science Fiction, Religion

Page Layout: There will be a series of interviews, documenting what the alternate universe is like, followed by an addendum showing how certain historical events have changed due to airplanes not being in wide use, and a final addendum that reveals its a world where God has deemed that humans are not allowed to leave the planet.

Elevator Pitch: This is an alternate dimension where man-made flight is essentially impossible, due to a phenomenon that occurs above a certain altitude (current thinking is about 6km up) that makes piloting and generally thinking rationally impossible.

Central Narrative: The story will show how the Foundations of both universes try to work together to discover the cause of the anomaly, as well as discover the differences in each other's histories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Much of the history of the 20th's century was shaped by the advent of air power. But what if air power was never a thing? Air craft carriers, strategic bombing, mail by air, even tourism would all completely change. This SCP will examine ways such a world might work.

Additional Notes: I've had this idea for a couple of years now, but I was never sure what to do with it. Recently, I remembered that there's a verse in the Quran that says:

"O assembly of jinns and men! If you have power to pass beyond the zones of the heavens and the earth, then pass (them)! But you will never be able to pass them, except with authority (from Allah)!"

Essentially, the cause is that in our world, God has allowed humanity to leave the heavens and earth, but in SCP-X, God has not allowed this.

item.title: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Personal horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous variation of Impostor Syndrome in which the affected person believes they are an actual impostor, stealing their own memories and identity. Severe cases might end up in the subject trying to kill themselves in an attempt at returning things to their right way.

Central Narrative: An up-and-coming Foundation researcher starts to conspire against themself, to the point of hiring a hitman to kill themself. This catches the attention of the psychiatric department and an investigation begins.
After several therapy sessions the affected researcher is put through a brain scan and the anomaly is found: it is an auto immune response to the constant contact the reaearcher had had with memetic and antimemetic material. It caused their brain to stop recognizing their own memories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
· An anomalous twist to an everyday problem, the Impostor Syndrome, a condition that causes a person to question their skills and value
· The concept of a memetic disease and a memetic immune system and how these interact with other memetic SCP articles and tales
· Potential long term characters and concepts to be used and explored by other articles and authors

Additional Notes: I haven't started writing it yet, this is the very first concept of my very first SCP article so I am open to all critics and suggestions :)
